CT CORONARY ANGIOGRAPHY

Clinical details: 58-year-old man. Exertional chest discomfort for 3 months, settles with rest. Ex-smoker. Treated hypertension.

Technique:
Non-contrast prospectively gated calcium score acquisition followed by prospectively ECG-triggered CT coronary angiography.
Heart rate 61 bpm, sinus rhythm. Metoprolol 10 mg IV. GTN 800 micrograms sublingual.
Contrast: Omnipaque 350, 65 ml.
DLP 168 mGy.cm (estimated effective dose 4.4 mSv).

Calcium score:
Total Agatston score 46 (LMS 0, LAD 46, LCx 0, RCA 0). 61st percentile for age, sex and ethnicity (MESA).

Coronary arteries:
Right dominant.
Normal coronary origins and course.
LMS: no plaque.
LAD: mixed plaque in the proximal segment with mild (25-49%) stenosis. No high-risk plaque features. Diagonals unremarkable.
LCx: no plaque. Obtuse marginals unremarkable.
RCA: no plaque.
No myocardial bridging.

Non-coronary findings:
Cardiac chambers normal in size. No pericardial effusion.
The left atrial appendage is well opacified with no filling defect to suggest thrombus.
Ascending aorta 34 mm. Pulmonary trunk 25 mm.
Visualised lung bases unremarkable. No significant extracardiac findings.

Conclusion:
1. Mild (25-49%) proximal LAD stenosis in mixed plaque without high-risk features. CAD-RADS 2/P1.
2. Optimisation of preventive therapy and risk factor modification is advised.
